questions.q: What are the three monitoring layers in the chapter's model?
options: CPU, memory, and disk
Backups, restores, and failover

Layer 1: infrastructure (CPU, memory, I/O, AG health); Layer 2: vector operations (DiskANN health, query latency, index size, pipeline lag); Layer 3: quality signals (recall@k probes, drift, user feedback)
Network, storage, and compute
questions.explain: The chapter's three-layer model: infrastructure metrics (existing SQL Server monitoring), vector-specific operational metrics (DiskANN health, Query Store vector latency, pipeline lag), and application-layer quality signals (recall probes, drift, user feedback) - Layer 3 being the one teams skip and regret.

questions.q: How often does the chapter's continuous recall probe run, and what does it check?
options: Once a day; it checks backup completion
Every 5 minutes; it runs a fixed set of queries with known-good answers (golden dataset) against the live retrieval path and records recall@k
Every hour; it rebuilds the DiskANN index
Once a week; it runs DBCC CHECKDB
questions.explain: The Python quality probe runs a fixed set of golden queries against the live retrieval path every 5 minutes (time.sleep(300)) and records recall@k plus top-1 distance - the earliest warning of index corruption, bad deployments, or embedding drift.

questions.q: Which condition pages the on-call engineer immediately (critical) in the chapter's alerting rules?
options: Recall@k probe drops more than 5 points sustained for 30 minutes, AG replica health = NOT_HEALTHY, or embedding queue depth growing for 30 minutes
A single slow query over 200ms
DiskANN index growth of 5% per day
Backup completing successfully
questions.explain: Critical (page immediately): recall@k probe drops >5 points for 30 minutes, AG health NOT_HEALTHY, or embedding queue depth growing for 30 minutes (ingest stalled). p99 >200ms and index growth >20%/day are only warnings.

questions.q: What warning-level threshold does the chapter set for vector query p99 latency?
options: p99 > 50ms for 1 minute
p99 > 1000ms for 1 hour
Any single query over 10ms
p99 > 200ms sustained for 10 minutes - ticket for business hours
questions.explain: Warning (business-hours ticket): vector query p99 latency >200ms for 10 minutes, alongside DiskANN index growth >20%/day, Pinecone index fullness >0.8, and probe top-1 distance trending up over 7 days.

questions.q: What Query Store retention does the chapter recommend for vector workloads, and why?
options: 7 days, to minimize storage
30 days, so latency trends survive long enough to correlate with recall-probe history
1 day, since probes replace it
Query Store should be off for vector workloads
questions.explain: Keep Query Store in read-write mode with 30-day retention for vector workloads so latency trends survive long enough to correlate with recall-probe history; this captures the full query load from all connections, not just instrumented ones.
